newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia reopens Indonesia border post.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia reopens Indonesia border post.

text.p: Malaysia has reopened a border post between its Sarawak state and Indonesia's West Kalimantan after recent riots in the Indonesian province, Malaysia's Bernama reported on Wednesday.
The news agency quoted Immigration Department public liaison officer Sarbini Hussein as saying the border post was reopened after discussions with government agencies.
"The Tebedu border post was officially reopened at 2 p.m. (0600 GMT)," he said on Wednesday from Sarawak's state capital of Kuching on Borneo island.

The Tebedu border post between Sarawak and Kalimantan was closed 10 days ago after clashes in West Kalimantan between Indonesia's native Dayaks and Moslem migrants from Madura island off Java's east coast.
It is among 12 border posts in Sarawak, all of which were closed because of the disturbances.
Sarawak, which along with Malaysia's Sabah state occupies the northern third of Borneo, while Indonesia has the southern two-thirds.
Officials were not immediately available to comment on the report and it was unclear if the remaining 11 posts were still closed.

Indonesian military officials and local residents say at least 12 people have been killed in the past six weeks from the fighting. Some residents and Church sources say the figure could be much higher.

Under Indonesia's controversial transmigration programme, tens of thousands of settlers from the overcrowded islands of Java and Madura have been shifted to less-populated areas such as Kalimantan and Sumatra island.
Last week, Indonesian military chief General Feisal Tanjung, said Malaysia had the right to close the 12 checkpoints on the border.
"Indonesia should respect the decision...," the official Indonesian Antara news agency quoted him as saying.
